contributions.changed: Exact zero leakage on the old subspace is a first-step property; it is not invariance under the enlarged retained evolution.
contributions.limitation: The 293-state space is not a complete electric-energy shell. Channel count alone does not prove the desired heat improvement.
contributions.next: Bound delayed occupation of the new channels before applying their remaining omitted coupling.
contributions.rationale: Promote the complete physical omitted image of P21 into the retained space, retaining its nonorthonormal Haar metric.

contributions.title: Improved ground certificate does not yet prove an improved heat bound
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Ground-state improvement and a documented failed coarse all-time error target.
contributions.changed: The historical AC1 gate correctly remains limited despite successful matrix assembly and a tighter ground certificate.
contributions.limitation: No implication from static ground improvement to the requested dynamic relative improvement.
contributions.next: Use the initially empty new channels and their actual loading equation.
contributions.rationale: Test the target quantity itself after enlarging the basis instead of substituting a better ground residual for a heat theorem.

contributions.title: Delayed channel loading closes the improved all-time relative bound
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Strict improvement over the Z2 physical all-time preparation-class certificate.
contributions.changed: The necessary improvement comes from the time ordering of physical channels, not the dimension 293 itself.
contributions.limitation: The input remains in the original P21 class. No all-input relative bound, real-time theorem, graph-size uniformity or executed solver for every coupling.
contributions.next: Execute the finite heat action with rigorous ground centering and numerical output error.
contributions.rationale: QLP_old=0 suppresses immediate escape, but the old-to-new-to-omitted route remains; integrate its new-channel amplitude.

contributions.title: Actual 293-coordinate heat at one declared time
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Executed 293-coordinate output with Haar metric, polynomial, centering and export errors accounted for.
contributions.changed: The heat theorem becomes a finite evaluated artifact at the fixed parameter-time-input contract.
contributions.limitation: AF1 executes one coupling, time and vacuum input only; it is not the all-time evaluator.
contributions.next: Prevent approximate centering from causing secular error and cover the full declared preparation class.
contributions.rationale: A physical Galerkin estimate does not certify the subsequently rounded and approximately centered vector.

contributions.title: Piecewise all-time computed heat and the fixed numerical scope
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Complete executed all-time finite-graph heat approximation on the declared preparation class.
contributions.changed: The early/late switch makes the error budget uniform while retaining a finite computation at requested rational times.
contributions.limitation: Fixed lambda=0.01 only. Reverse CLI accepts real rational 293-vectors, with 11e-30 rounding; complex operator bounds and forward complex demonstrations use the separate 15e-40 allowance, not an arbitrary-complex CLI. A tiny switch discontinuity is allowed within budget.
contributions.next: Validate graph-size or observable dependence and an explicit physical scale-identification contract; do not infer continuum or calibration results.
contributions.rationale: An approximate ground energy cannot be multiplied by unbounded time; late heat should be replaced by a certified ground projector.

contributions.title: Canonical rank observable has an actual eight-link first-order resonance
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: A concrete nonzero secular coefficient for the canonical summable family.
contributions.changed: This supplies a physical-model resonance mechanism rather than a two-level analogy, while leaving higher bulk terms unresolved at U1.
contributions.limitation: Rank-two bounded operator, not Wilson multiplication. U1 is limited and has only same-author self-review. No exact endpoint limit yet.
contributions.next: Bound all connected higher orders of the full model uniformly on the stated endpoint window.
contributions.rationale: Construct a gauge-invariant observable whose created vector lies in an actual resonant electric-energy sector.

contributions.title: Full-system endpoint witness from connected-word tails
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: A full-model counterexample to extending the earlier subcritical window to the critical cubic time exponent for every bounded local probe.
contributions.changed: The gamma=3 endpoint obstruction is established in the frozen canonical model; it is not merely a formal secular term.
contributions.limitation: Existence of a suitable probe, not a universal statement for all observables. No exact trajectory at U2, Wilson measurement or physical scale calibration. Same-author self-review.
contributions.next: Provide an operational readout and prove an actual scalar limit using controlled spatial collars.
contributions.rationale: A local first-order coefficient only becomes an endpoint theorem after controlling full bulk higher orders and stationary-state replacement.

contributions.title: Finite-outcome and coherent readout of the complex correlation
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: An ideal coherent measurement contract with explicit operator approximation tolerance.
contributions.changed: Finite outcome count does not establish a finite laboratory implementation; complex order must be measured coherently.
contributions.limitation: Ideal bounded operators and controlled unitaries are assumed, not physically calibrated or implemented.
contributions.next: Include clock, state, gate and statistical errors in the same correlation budget.
contributions.rationale: A noncommuting two-time complex correlation is not recovered by an ordinary sequential PVM without disturbing the relevant coherence.

contributions.title: Full-Haar operator-norm obstruction to multiplying-observable replacement
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Rules out an unjustified identification of the original rank observable with Wilson multiplication.
contributions.changed: Same vacuum-created vector or a formal compressed agreement does not imply that the complete observables are equal.
contributions.limitation: This full-space norm obstruction does not forbid separately analyzing a Wilson multiplier or a declared restricted norm.
contributions.next: Construct and certify a Wilson observable on its own operator and state contract.
contributions.rationale: A proposed easier multiplication readout must approximate the actual rank observable in the norm used by the witness theorem.

contributions.title: Clock and finite-sample error budget for the coherent protocol
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: A complete ideal-protocol error and shot-count certificate at explicit finite q.
contributions.changed: Operational tolerances are mathematically quantified and can be extremely demanding even when the ideal signal is nonzero.
contributions.limitation: Sufficient theoretical budget, not evidence of experimental attainability. State, gate and timing conventions differ between directions and are not interchangeable.
contributions.next: Find feasible apparatus-specific approximations with a justified physical scale calibration.
contributions.rationale: The physical clock error must be propagated through an actual bounded commutator, not the size of the long elapsed time alone.

contributions.title: Complete-factor spatial collars with factorial connected tails
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Finite spatial reduction with explicit error that preserves the endpoint signal.
contributions.changed: A controlled physical collar replaces an arbitrary geometric crop; its small tail does not by itself justify averaging the regional spectrum.
contributions.limitation: Collars and counts depend on the stated forward/reverse construction. No regional matrix or infinite limiting generator is computed at this stage.
contributions.next: Establish strong averaging on fixed energy blocks and then pass the scalar limit through the collar bound.
contributions.rationale: All interaction factors touching the explored support must be retained before counting escaping connected words.

contributions.title: Actual scalar endpoint limit from strong block averaging
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: An actual limiting endpoint function with quantitative small-window location.
contributions.changed: U2 nonconvergence is strengthened to existence of the relevant scalar limit; the whole energy shell and the q=1 global generator are not thereby constructed.
contributions.limitation: Fixed small window, scalar limit and strong block topology. Compact resolvent is not a global operator-norm averaging theorem.
contributions.next: Compute a reducing reached component or else retain the full regional energy block.
contributions.rationale: Strong finite-energy averaging and uniform scalar collar errors permit sequential limits without claiming global operator-norm convergence.

contributions.title: Exact sixteen-cycle compression and spectral measure
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: An exact finite spectral candidate for the endpoint function.
contributions.changed: An autonomous two-state approximation is replaced by the correct sixteen-state compression, while exterior closure remains an explicit missing hypothesis at AA1.
contributions.limitation: AA1 gate is limited. The cube compression alone does not transfer to the surrounding or full model. Same-author serial self-review, not independent review.
contributions.next: Prove that exterior faces cannot return resonantly into the shell and identify a reducing reached component.
contributions.rationale: The original two-cycle span is not invariant; enumerate the complete physical cube shell and diagonalize its reached graph.

contributions.title: Exterior selection proves the reached component reduces
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Transfers the exact spectral measure to the actual canonical endpoint scalar on the admitted window.
contributions.changed: AA1 compression becomes a full-model result because exterior resonant escape is excluded, not because the entire energy shell is finite.
contributions.limitation: Only the reached component of the averaged generator is reducing; instantaneous evolution can leave it. No large-z stationary-limit claim follows from the analytic formula. Same-author review.
contributions.next: Attach finite-q and arithmetic errors to the full correlation and analyze simpler multiplier probes.
contributions.rationale: Full surrounding-factor ownership and energy selection are needed to justify the finite spectral formula.

contributions.title: Finite-q approach and numerical endpoint enclosure
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: An explicit finite-q scalar enclosure for the original rank observable.
contributions.changed: The endpoint spectral formula is accompanied by an actual full-model finite-q error budget.
contributions.limitation: Numerical point is extremely close to q=1 and has an enormous uncalibrated physical duration. No experimental feasibility or larger-z theorem.
contributions.next: Check the same full finite-q transfer for actual Wilson multipliers with their own operator norms.
contributions.rationale: A limiting formula must be connected to a finite parameter value, the true stationary state, a finite collar and finite arithmetic.

contributions.title: Nonzero-variance elementary Wilson probe is endpoint-null
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: A physical-model null control against inferring a slow coupling from a constant phase-removed scalar.
contributions.changed: Nonzero variance and an apparently clean signal are insufficient for scale identification; this probe has no endpoint sensitivity to that coupling.
contributions.limitation: AD1 remains limited as a rate-bridge target. A constant endpoint does not rule out subleading finite-q dependence or sensitivity of another observable.
contributions.next: Choose a Wilson multiplier whose created vector reaches a nontrivial averaged block and prove the full scalar transfer.
contributions.rationale: Variance measures creation of a state, while endpoint sensitivity requires nontrivial averaged dynamics on that state.

contributions.title: Informative single-cycle and sum Wilson endpoints
contributions.status: model-specific derivation, obstruction, or certified computation
contributions.application: Actual Wilson-multiplication probes with quadratic or linear small-window endpoint sensitivity.
contributions.changed: The rank observable is no longer silently identified with multiplication; different physical observables can share an endpoint spectral component yet differ as operators.
contributions.limitation: Fixed canonical summable model and 0<z<=1e-6. The coefficient is not an empirical coupling calibration, and no large-z limit or homogeneous/continuum transfer is proved.
contributions.next: Declare the observable, clock, physical scales and comparison norm in an actual parameter-identification experiment.
contributions.rationale: Shared vacuum-created states permit the reached spectral calculation, but each full multiplier still requires its own norm and finite-q budget.
